title: Around town: autos, cabs & the metro
goal: Haggle with an auto driver, tell a driver where to go, stop and drop you, book and ride a cab, find your way on the metro, and ask how long a trip takes.
intro:
Getting around a Telugu city is a conversation: you agree a fare with the auto driver (**ఎంత తీసుకుంటారు?**), read out the OTP to the cab driver, direct them from the back seat (**సిగ్నల్ దగ్గర లెఫ్ట్ తీసుకోండి**) and tell them exactly where to stop (**ఇక్కడే, ఇక్కడే! ఆపేయండి**).

The grammar here is the grammar of moving: **pairs of verbs** like *ఆగు* (come to a stop) and *ఆపు* (stop something), *దిగు* (get off) and *దింపు* (drop someone off), and **compound verbs** with *-ఏయ్* ('do it right now') and *-పో* ('away, off'). You'll also learn to say how long something takes with **పడుతుంది**. Drivers get **మీరు** and **-ండి**, and are usually called **అన్నా** ('brother').

vocab.note: ఆటో బాడుగ = auto fare · in Telangana and Hyderabad people say కిరాయి
ఎక్స్‌ట్రా ఇవ్వాలి = you have to pay extra
Transitive partner of దిగు (get off): నన్ను ఇక్కడ దింపండి = drop me here
Transitive partner of ఆగు (come to a stop): ఇక్కడ ఆపండి = stop here · ఆపేయండి = just stop
English loan, more common in speech than చిరునామా
సిగ్నల్ దాటాక = after the signal · రోడ్డు దాటు = cross the road
Transitive partner of తిరుగు: ఊరంతా తిప్పాడు = he took me all round town

vocab.en: to drive, ride (a vehicle); to run (a business)
vocab.note: నెమ్మదిగా నడపండి = drive slowly · past: నడిపాను
Cab drivers ask for it at the start of the ride: ఓటీపీ చెప్పండి
లైన్ మారాలి = you have to change lines · లైన్‌లో నిలబడు = stand in the queue
For time: non-past పడుతుంది (it takes), past పట్టింది (it took)

I've no change, can I pay by PhonePe?
phrases.note: Or జీపే (Google Pay): UPI QR codes are everywhere

phrases.en: Drop me at the station, please.
Take a left at the signal.
phrases.note: Drivers use English లెఫ్ట్ / రైట్ (raiṭ) more than ఎడమ / కుడి

At this time of day it'll take an hour.

grammar.title: Verb pairs and compound verbs: ఆగు / ఆపు, దిగు / దింపు, -ఏయ్, -పో
grammar.body:
**Verb pairs.** Many Telugu verbs come in pairs: one for 'it happens' and one for 'someone makes it happen'.
• **ఆగు** (come to a stop, wait) / **ఆపు** (stop something): *బస్సు ఆగింది* (the bus stopped) / *ఇక్కడ ఆపండి* (stop [the car] here)
• **దిగు** (get off, get down) / **దింపు** (drop someone off): *నేను ఇక్కడ దిగుతా* / *నన్ను ఇక్కడ దింపండి*
• **ఎక్కు** (get on) / **ఎక్కించు** (put on, let on board)
• **తిరుగు** (turn, go round) / **తిప్పు** (turn something, take someone round)
The trap: *ఇక్కడ ఆగండి* to a driver can mean 'wait here'; *ఇక్కడ ఆపండి* is the clear 'stop here'.

**Compound verbs.** Telugu adds a second verb to the *-ఇ* form to colour the meaning:
• **-ఏయ్ / -ఏస్-** (from వేయు, 'throw'): do it **right away, completely, decisively**: *ఆపేయండి* (just stop!), *దింపేయ్* (just drop me), *తినేయ్* (eat it up), *వచ్చేస్తా* (I'll be right there). Past: *ఆపేశాడు*.
• **-ఇపో** (from పోవు, 'go'): **away, off, it's happened**: *దిగిపో* (get off!), *వెళ్ళిపోయింది* (it's left, it's gone), *అయిపోయింది* (it's over), *మారిపోయింది* (it's changed completely).
• **-కో** (for oneself): *తీసుకో* (take for yourself), *ఎక్కించుకో* (take a passenger on).

examples.en: The bus has stopped, get off!
Just drop me at the metro station. (to a friend)
Oh no, the bus has gone!
The auto guy took me all round town.

grammar.title: How long it takes, how far, how much: పడుతుంది, అవుతుంది
grammar.body:
**Time taken** uses **పట్టు** ('take, hold') with the time as the subject: *అరగంట పడుతుంది* (it takes half an hour), past *గంట పట్టింది* (it took an hour). Note the forms: non-past **పడుతుంది** (paḍutundi), past **పట్టింది** (paṭṭindi). Ask: *ఎంత సేపు పడుతుంది?* The person it took goes in the dative: *నాకు గంట పట్టింది* (it took me an hour).

**Cost** uses **అవు** ('become'): *ఎంత అవుతుంది?* (how much will it come to?), *వంద అవుతుంది*, past *నాలుగు వందలు అయింది* (it came to four hundred).

**Distance**: *ఎంత దూరం?* (how far?), *ఐదు కిలోమీటర్లు*, *ఇంకెంత దూరం?* (how much further?).

**In / within** a time is **-లో**: *పది నిమిషాల్లో*, *అరగంటలో*; **by** a time is **కల్లా** (Unit 21).

The trap: don't translate 'it takes' with తీసుకో. *గంట తీసుకుంటుంది* is heard from English speakers, but *గంట పడుతుంది* is what Telugu speakers say.

examples.en: It takes an hour and a half from here to the airport.

examples.native: వైజాగ్ నుంచి విజయవాడకి రైల్లో ఆరు గంటలు పడుతుంది.
examples.roman: vaijāg nunchi vijayavāḍaki raillō āru gaṇṭalu paḍutundi.
examples.en: It takes six hours by train from Vizag to Vijayawada.
By metro it only takes twenty minutes.
The cab came to four hundred.
The beach is three kilometres from here.

dialogue.title: An auto to Jubilee Hills
dialogue.setting: Hyderabad, rush hour. Keerthi flags down an auto at Ameerpet.

lines.speaker: Keerthi
lines.en: Auto! Will you go to Jubilee Hills Checkpost?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: I'll go, madam. It'll be two-fifty.

lines.speaker: Keerthi
lines.en: That much? Go by the meter.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: మీటర్ పని చేయట్లేదు మేడం. ఈ టైంలో ట్రాఫిక్ ఎక్కువ, పైగా తిరిగి ఖాళీగా రావాలి.
lines.roman: mīṭar pani chēyaṭlēdu mēḍam. ī ṭaimlō ṭrāphik ekkuva, paigā tirigi khāḷīgā rāvāli.
lines.en: The meter isn't working, madam. There's lots of traffic at this hour, and on top of that I have to come back empty.

lines.speaker: Keerthi
lines.native: రోజూ వెళ్తా, నూట యాభై అవుతుంది. నూట ఎనభై ఇస్తా.
lines.roman: rōjū veḷtā, nūṭa yābhai avutundi. nūṭa enabhai istā.
lines.en: I go every day, it comes to one-fifty. I'll give you one-eighty.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: Give me two hundred, madam, final.

lines.speaker: Keerthi
lines.native: సరే, పదండి. ఫ్లైఓవర్ మీద నుంచి వెళ్ళండి, తొందరగా వెళ్ళాలి.
lines.roman: sarē, padaṇḍi. phlaiōvar mīda nunchi veḷḷaṇḍi, tondaragā veḷḷāli.
lines.en: OK, let's go. Take the flyover, I need to get there quickly.

lines.speaker: Keerthi
lines.en: (Ten minutes later) Anna, why are you turning into this lane?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: ముందు రోడ్డు మీద పెద్ద జామ్ మేడం. ఇది షార్ట్‌కట్.
lines.roman: mundu rōḍḍu mīda pedda jām mēḍam. idi ṣārṭkaṭ.
lines.en: There's a big jam on the main road ahead, madam. This is a shortcut.

lines.speaker: Keerthi
lines.native: సరే. ఆ సిగ్నల్ దాటాక లెఫ్ట్ తీసుకోండి... ఆ, ఇక్కడే, ఇక్కడే! ఆపేయండి.
lines.roman: sarē. ā signal dāṭāka lephṭ tīsukōṇḍi... ā, ikkaḍē, ikkaḍē! āpēyaṇḍi.
lines.en: OK. Take a left after that signal... yes, here, right here! Stop.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: ఇక్కడ ఆపితే పోలీసులు ఫైన్ వేస్తారు. కొంచెం ముందు దింపుతా.
lines.roman: ikkaḍa āpitē pōlīsulu phain vēstāru. konchem mundu dimputā.
lines.en: If I stop here the police will fine me. I'll drop you a bit further on.

lines.speaker: Keerthi
lines.en: OK. I've no change, can I PhonePe you?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: Go ahead, madam, here's the QR code.

culture: Auto drivers in Hyderabad often refuse to use the meter, especially at rush hour or for one-way trips, so agree the fare before you get in; ride apps (Ola, Uber, and Rapido for bike taxis and autos) have made prices more predictable, and drivers will ask for the **OTP** before starting. In Vijayawada and Vizag, **share autos** run fixed routes for a few rupees and squeeze in far more passengers than seems possible. The **Hyderabad Metro** has three lines meeting at Ameerpet and MG Bus Station, with a women's coach at the front; buy a token or top up a card. Speak to drivers politely with *మీరు* and *-ండి*; call a driver *అన్నా* ('brother') or, if older, *బాబాయ్* ('uncle'), and they'll call you *సార్* or *మేడం*. Directions are given by landmarks rather than street names (*ఆ పెట్రోల్ బంకు దగ్గర*, *సిగ్నల్ దాటాక*), and almost everyone pays by UPI: *ఫోన్‌పే చేయనా?*

tip.title: Agree the fare first
tip.body:
- Use **మీరు** and **-ండి** with drivers; call them **అన్నా**.
- Ask first: **ఎంత తీసుకుంటారు?** Then **మీటర్ మీద రండి**, or make an offer: **…ఇస్తా** 'I'll give…'.
- Too much: **చాలా ఎక్కువ** · final price: **చివరి ధర**.

sentences.en: How much to Benz Circle?
Anna, will you go to the bus station?
What's the auto fare?
Go by the meter, I won't pay extra.
At night they ask for extra.
That's too much, I'll give you one-fifty.
It's only ten rupees in a share auto.
OK, tell me your final price.
I've no change, anna, can I pay by PhonePe?

tip.title: Stop vs stop it: ఆగు / ఆపు, దిగు / దింపు
tip.body:
- **ఆగు** = come to a stop · **ఆపు** = stop something: బస్సు **ఆగింది** / ఇక్కడ **ఆపండి**.
- **దిగు** = get off · **దింపు** = drop someone off: నేను **దిగుతా** / నన్ను **దింపండి**.
- Same pattern: ఎక్కు / ఎక్కించు, తిరుగు / తిప్పు.

sentences.en: Drop me at the temple, please.
I'll get off right here.
Anna, pull over a bit, please.
Does the bus stop here?
Take me to this address, please.
I'll drop the kids at school and come.

sentences.native: ఇక్కడే, ఇక్కడే! ఆ గేట్ దగ్గర ఆపండి.
sentences.roman: ikkaḍē, ikkaḍē! ā gēṭ daggara āpaṇḍi.
sentences.en: Here, right here! Stop by that gate.
I've sent the address on WhatsApp.
Will you drop me home tonight? (to a friend)

tip.title: Do it now: -ఏయ్ · away, off: -పో
tip.body:
- **-ఏయ్** (from వేయు) = right away, completely: **ఆపేయండి** 'just stop', **దింపేయ్** 'just drop me'.
- **-ఇపో** (from పోవు) = off, away, done: **దిగిపో** 'get off', **వెళ్ళిపోయింది** 'it's gone'.
- **తిరుగు** = turn, go round · **తిప్పు** = turn something, take someone round.

sentences.en: Just stop after the signal.
Don't take the flyover, go underneath.
Do a U-turn here.
Anna, why are you taking me the long way round?
I know a shortcut, I'll show you the way.
Drive a bit slower, please, there are kids with us.
Cross the road and get an auto on the other side.

sentences.native: రెండో సిగ్నల్ దగ్గర లెఫ్ట్, తర్వాత నేరుగా.
sentences.roman: reṇḍō signal daggara lephṭ, tarvāta nērugā.
sentences.en: Left at the second signal, then straight on.
This is our lane, let's get out here.

tip.title: Ride apps
tip.body:
- Book: **క్యాబ్ / ఆటో బుక్ చేయు** · the driver asks **ఓటీపీ చెప్పండి**.
- Drivers call you **సార్ / మేడం**; you call them **అన్నా** and use **-ండి**.
- The ride's cost: **ఎంత అయింది?** · distance: **ఎంత దూరం?**, **…కిలోమీటర్లు**.

sentences.native: క్యాబ్ బుక్ చేయనా, ఆటో బుక్ చేయనా?
sentences.roman: kyāb buk chēyanā, āṭō buk chēyanā?
sentences.en: Shall I book a cab or an auto?

sentences.native: డ్రైవర్ ఎక్కడ ఉన్నాడు? ఐదు నిమిషాల్లో వస్తాడట.
sentences.roman: ḍraivar ekkaḍa unnāḍu? aidu nimiṣāllō vastāḍaṭa.
sentences.en: Where's the driver? Apparently he'll be here in five minutes.
Sir, tell me the OTP, please.
The driver cancelled the ride!
How much did this ride come to?

sentences.native: క్యాబ్ బుక్ చేశా, గేట్ దగ్గర వెయిట్ చెయ్.
sentences.roman: kyāb buk chēshā, gēṭ daggara veyiṭ chey.
sentences.en: I've booked a cab, wait at the gate.

sentences.native: మీ లొకేషన్ షేర్ చేయండి సార్, అడ్రస్ దొరకట్లేదు.
sentences.roman: mī lokēṣan ṣēr chēyaṇḍi sār, aḍras dorakaṭlēdu.
sentences.en: Please share your location, sir, I can't find the address.
How much further? Another two kilometres.

sentences.native: మా ఆఫీసు ఇక్కడి నుంచి పది కిలోమీటర్లు.
sentences.roman: mā āphīsu ikkaḍi nunchi padi kilōmīṭarlu.
sentences.en: My office is ten kilometres from here.
Sir, you've put in the wrong address.

tip.title: It takes: పడుతుంది / పట్టింది
tip.body:
- Time is the subject of **పట్టు**: గంట **పడుతుంది** 'it takes an hour' · గంట **పట్టింది** 'it took an hour'.
- Who it took: dative: **నాకు** గంట పట్టింది.
- In (a time): **-లో**: అరగంట**లో** · cost: **ఎంత అవుతుంది?**

sentences.en: How long does it take to Ameerpet by metro?
It takes an hour from home to the office.

sentences.native: నిన్న ట్రాఫిక్‌లో నాకు రెండు గంటలు పట్టింది.
sentences.roman: ninna ṭrāphiklō nāku reṇḍu gaṇṭalu paṭṭindi.
sentences.en: Yesterday it took me two hours in the traffic.

sentences.native: సాయంత్రం ఈ టైంలో హైటెక్ సిటీకి గంట పడుతుంది.
sentences.roman: sāyantram ī ṭaimlō haiṭek siṭīki gaṇṭa paḍutundi.
sentences.en: At this time in the evening it takes an hour to Hitech City.
How much is a metro token?
By cab you can get there in half an hour.
One token to LB Nagar, please.
You have to change lines at Ameerpet.
What's the next stop?

sentences.native: ఉదయం మెట్రోలో చాలా రద్దీ, సీటు దొరకదు.
sentences.roman: udayam meṭrōlō chālā raddī, sīṭu dorakadu.
sentences.en: The metro's packed in the morning, you won't get a seat.

sentences.native: హైటెక్ సిటీకి వెళ్ళాలంటే ఏ స్టేషనులో మారాలి?
sentences.roman: haiṭek siṭīki veḷḷālaṇṭē ē sṭēṣanulō mārāli?
sentences.en: To get to Hitech City, which station do I change at?
